newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung appointed to Deng's funeral committee.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung appointed to Deng's funeral committee.

text.p: Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa has been appointed a member of Deng Xiaoping's funeral committee, China's official Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

Tung, a Shanghai-born shipping magnate anointed as Hong Kong's future leader in December, is in Beijing to report to Chinese leaders on his choice of top officials to serve when the British leave later this year.
Tung arrived in the Chinese capital hours before Deng's death on Wednesday and is scheduled to return to Hong Kong on Thursday.
It was not immediately clear whether he would change his plans and delay the announcement of his team of officials.
Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30 when more than 150 years of British colonial rule end.
China has promised the territory of 6.3 million people considerable autonomy after the handover under Deng's "One Country, Two Systems" concept.

In neighbouring Macau, the Xinhua News Agency, Beijing's de facto embassy there, said it would set up an altar for the people of the Portuguese-run territory to pay their respects to the paramount leader. Macau reverts to China in 1999.
The 459-member funeral committee will be led by Communist Party chief and President Jiang Zemin, Deng's anointed successor.
